common_name: The Fairy Polyantha Rose (Low, Spreading Pink Ground Cover Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown, own-root shrubs in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; The Fairy is a low, spreading polyantha rose useful as a flowering ground cover or low border.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun; the low, spreading habit works well as a flowering ground cover, low informal hedge, or the front of a mixed border. The Fairy produces dense clusters of small, double, soft pink rosette blooms almost continuously from late spring through fall, on a compact, glossy-leaved shrub that is exceptionally disease-resistant and easy to grow without spraying. Its long bloom season and low maintenance have made it one of the most widely planted polyantha roses in modern gardens. Deadhead spent clusters to encourage continued rebloom, and prune lightly in late winter to maintain shape.

common_name: Cecile Brunner Rose (Sweetheart Rose, Miniature Pink Polyantha)

planting.note: Plant container-grown, own-root shrubs in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Cecile Brunner, the classic Sweetheart Rose, bears tiny, perfectly formed pink buds long favored for boutonnieres and corsages.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun. Cecile Brunner, known widely as the Sweetheart Rose, produces small clusters of perfectly formed, tiny, soft pink buds that open into miniature, high-centered blooms with a light, sweet fragrance, long prized for buttonholes, corsages, and small posies. The bush form blooms repeatedly through the season on a compact, well-mannered shrub, while a climbing sport of the same cultivar can reach twenty feet or more where space allows. Deadhead spent blooms to encourage continued flowering, and prune lightly in late winter to maintain a tidy shape.

common_name: Marie Pavie Rose (Fragrant White Polyantha Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown, own-root shrubs in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Marie Pavie is a compact, fragrant white polyantha rose that blooms almost continuously.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun. Marie Pavie bears small clusters of double, blush-white blooms with a notably strong, sweet fragrance for a polyantha, opening from soft pink buds on a compact, tidy, nearly thornless shrub that flowers almost without pause from late spring through hard frost. Its combination of fragrance, near-continuous bloom, and compact habit has made it a long-standing favorite for edging beds and small gardens. Deadhead spent clusters to encourage continued rebloom, and prune lightly in late winter to maintain shape.

common_name: Hansa Rugosa Rose (Fragrant Reddish-Purple Rugosa Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown, own-root shrubs in spring in average, well-drained sandy soil in full sun; Hansa is an old, exceptionally cold-hardy, fragrant rugosa rose that tolerates poor, sandy, and coastal soils.

directions: Plant in average to sandy, well-drained soil in full sun; rugosa roses excel in poor, dry, or coastal soils that would stress most other roses. Hansa bears large, double, reddish-purple blooms with an intensely strong, clove-like fragrance, followed by large, showy orange-red hips that provide fall and winter interest and attract birds. The rugged, wrinkled-leaved shrub is exceptionally cold-hardy and disease-resistant, tolerating salt spray and poor soil better than nearly any other rose class. Prune only lightly to remove dead wood, since rugosas bloom on both old and new growth and resent hard pruning.

common_name: Blanc Double de Coubert Rose (Fragrant Pure White Rugosa Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown, own-root shrubs in spring in average, well-drained sandy soil in full sun; Blanc Double de Coubert is a fragrant white rugosa rose noted for its papery, crepe-textured petals.

directions: Plant in average to sandy, well-drained soil in full sun; rugosa roses excel in poor, dry, or coastal soils that would stress most other roses. Blanc Double de Coubert bears large, loosely double, pure white blooms with a papery, crepe-like petal texture and a strong, sweet fragrance, opening against the rugged, deeply veined rugosa foliage that stays clean and disease-free through the season. The vigorous shrub is exceptionally cold-hardy and salt-tolerant, useful for coastal plantings and difficult, sandy sites. Prune only lightly to remove dead wood, since rugosas bloom on both old and new growth and resent hard pruning.

common_name: Roseraie de l'Hay Rose (Fragrant Wine-Red Rugosa Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown, own-root shrubs in spring in average, well-drained sandy soil in full sun; Roseraie de l'Hay is a vigorous, intensely fragrant wine-red rugosa rose named for the famed French rose garden.

directions: Plant in average to sandy, well-drained soil in full sun; rugosa roses excel in poor, dry, or coastal soils that would stress most other roses. Roseraie de l'Hay bears large, loosely double, rich wine-red to magenta blooms with an intense, spicy-sweet fragrance considered among the strongest of any rugosa, opening on a large, vigorous shrub that can be used as an informal flowering hedge. It sets few hips compared to other rugosas since its heavily petaled blooms are less fertile, so it is grown primarily for its exceptional flower color and fragrance. Prune only lightly to remove dead wood, since rugosas bloom on both old and new growth and resent hard pruning.

common_name: Frau Dagmar Hartopp Rugosa Rose (Silvery-Pink Single Rugosa Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown, own-root shrubs in spring in average, well-drained sandy soil in full sun; Frau Dagmar Hartopp is a compact, single-flowered pink rugosa rose grown for both bloom and its large, showy hips.

directions: Plant in average to sandy, well-drained soil in full sun; rugosa roses excel in poor, dry, or coastal soils that would stress most other roses. Frau Dagmar Hartopp bears single, silvery-pink blooms with prominent cream-colored stamens and a light, sweet fragrance, followed by unusually large, showy, tomato-red hips that persist into winter and provide strong multi-season interest along with reliable fall color from the foliage. Its compact size compared to many rugosas suits it to smaller gardens and low informal hedging. Prune only lightly to remove dead wood, since rugosas bloom on both old and new growth and resent hard pruning.

common_name: Rugosa Alba Rose (Wild Single White Rugosa Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown, own-root shrubs in spring in average, well-drained sandy soil in full sun; Rugosa Alba is the classic wild white-flowered form of the species rose, prized for coastal and dune plantings.

directions: Plant in average to sandy, well-drained soil in full sun; this is one of the toughest roses available for dune stabilization, coastal exposure, and salt-affected soils. Rugosa Alba bears large, single, pure white blooms with golden stamens and a strong, clove-like fragrance, followed by exceptionally large, tomato-red hips prized both ornamentally and for high vitamin-C content used in jams and teas. The rugged, deeply wrinkled foliage stays clean through the growing season and often turns gold in fall. Prune only lightly to remove dead wood, since rugosas bloom on both old and new growth and resent hard pruning.

common_name: Buffalo Gal Rugosa Rose (Low, Spreading Pink Ground Cover Rugosa Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown, own-root shrubs in spring in average, well-drained sandy soil in full sun; Buffalo Gal is a low, spreading rugosa hybrid useful as a tough, drought-tolerant ground cover.

directions: Plant in average to sandy, well-drained soil in full sun; the low, wide-spreading habit makes it useful as a tough, drought-tolerant flowering ground cover on slopes or in difficult sandy sites. Buffalo Gal bears single to semi-double, deep pink blooms with a light fragrance in repeated flushes through the growing season, on a low, dense, rugosa-type shrub that inherits the parent species' outstanding disease resistance and salt tolerance. Its spreading form works well cascading over a low wall or covering a sunny bank. Prune only lightly to remove dead wood and maintain shape, since rugosa-type roses resent hard pruning.

common_name: Penelope Hybrid Musk Rose (Fragrant Creamy Apricot-Pink Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown, own-root shrubs in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Penelope is a classic, richly fragrant hybrid musk shrub rose that tolerates a bit of shade.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; hybrid musk roses tolerate more shade than most rose classes, blooming reasonably well with just a half-day of direct sun. Penelope bears large clusters of semi-double, creamy apricot-pink blooms fading to soft white, with a strong, musky-sweet fragrance carried well beyond the plant itself, followed in fall by coral-pink hips if left undeadheaded late in the season. The lax, arching shrub repeats bloom reliably through the growing season and can be trained as a short climber against a wall. Prune back by about a third in late winter and deadhead through summer to encourage continued flowering.

common_name: Buff Beauty Hybrid Musk Rose (Fragrant Apricot-Buff Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown, own-root shrubs in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Buff Beauty is a fragrant, apricot-buff hybrid musk shrub rose that tolerates a bit of shade.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; hybrid musk roses tolerate more shade than most rose classes, blooming reasonably well with just a half-day of direct sun. Buff Beauty bears large clusters of double, warm apricot-buff blooms that soften as they age, with a strong, musky-sweet fragrance and coppery new foliage that adds color even before the flowers open. The lax, spreading shrub repeats bloom well through the growing season and can be trained as a short climber against a wall or fence for extra height. Prune back by about a third in late winter and deadhead through summer to encourage continued flowering.

common_name: Cornelia Hybrid Musk Rose (Fragrant Coral-Pink Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown, own-root shrubs in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Cornelia is a fragrant, coral-pink hybrid musk shrub rose that tolerates a bit of shade.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; hybrid musk roses tolerate more shade than most rose classes, blooming reasonably well with just a half-day of direct sun. Cornelia bears large clusters of small, double, coral-pink blooms speckled with yellow at the base, with a strong, musky-sweet fragrance, opening against dark, glossy foliage on a vigorous, arching shrub. It repeats bloom well through the growing season and, like other hybrid musks, can be trained as a short climber against a wall or fence for extra height. Prune back by about a third in late winter and deadhead through summer to encourage continued flowering.

common_name: Felicia Hybrid Musk Rose (Fragrant Silvery-Pink Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown, own-root shrubs in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Felicia is a fragrant, silvery-pink hybrid musk shrub rose that tolerates a bit of shade.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; hybrid musk roses tolerate more shade than most rose classes, blooming reasonably well with just a half-day of direct sun. Felicia bears large clusters of double, silvery-pink blooms with soft salmon undertones and a strong, musky-sweet fragrance, opening on a dense, well-rounded shrub considered one of the most reliably floriferous hybrid musks. It repeats bloom well through the growing season and works equally well as a freestanding shrub or informal flowering hedge. Prune back by about a third in late winter and deadhead through summer to encourage continued flowering.

common_name: Prosperity Hybrid Musk Rose (Fragrant White Cluster-Flowered Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown, own-root shrubs in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Prosperity is a fragrant, white-flowered hybrid musk shrub rose that tolerates a bit of shade.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; hybrid musk roses tolerate more shade than most rose classes, blooming reasonably well with just a half-day of direct sun. Prosperity bears large, dense clusters of double, creamy white blooms tinged with pale pink in bud, with a strong, musky-sweet fragrance, opening against glossy dark foliage on a dense, rounded shrub. It repeats bloom well through the growing season and its pale color makes it a versatile choice for a white or moon garden. Prune back by about a third in late winter and deadhead through summer to encourage continued flowering.

common_name: Will Scarlet Hybrid Musk Rose (Vivid Scarlet-Red Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown, own-root shrubs in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Will Scarlet is a vivid scarlet-red sport of the pink hybrid musk Skyrocket, tolerating a bit of shade.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; hybrid musk roses tolerate more shade than most rose classes, blooming reasonably well with just a half-day of direct sun. Will Scarlet, a vivid scarlet-red sport of the hybrid musk Skyrocket, bears large clusters of semi-double blooms with a light, musky fragrance and golden stamens, opening on a tall, vigorous shrub that can be trained as a short climber against a wall or fence. It repeats bloom well through the growing season and often sets attractive orange hips in fall if lightly deadheaded. Prune back by about a third in late winter to shape and encourage vigorous new flowering wood.
